question.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
question.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(2,-5,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-5,3⟩,$ and $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =⟨2,-5,3⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =-21.\end{aligned}
$$
